structured.finding: No requirement says what happens when tool_choice has an unsupported type (such as an int). A requirement would say such input must be rejected with a TypeError, not passed on silently as None.
structured.reason: The mutant no longer raises for tool_choice values that are not a string, mapping or None. It returns None instead of raising TypeError, which a caller can see. REQ_TOOL_CHOICE only covers named choices and "required", so nothing says how unsupported input types must be rejected.
sources: Both supported public named-choice input forms normalize to the same selected registered tool.
msg = "tool_choice must be a string, mapping, or None."
When the caller explicitly selects a named tool, a supported provider route shall request and execute that tool rather than silently choosing another registered tool.
